Attach labels to a scale

Source: R/labels.R
attach_labels_scale.Rd

Adds display names to the object's label table. A label belongs to a member (frame, member) and to a variant – a free name such as "name", "short" or a language code – so a member may carry several. The table is sparse: frames and members without a row are shown by their code. A row with member = NA labels the frame itself.

Usage

attach_labels_scale(
  x,
  labels,
  variant = NULL,
  default = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A NestedScale.

labels

A data.frame with columns frame, member, label and, unless variant is given, optionally variant.

variant

Single string filled into the variant column when labels has none. Defaults to "label".

default

Single string naming the variant used when a lookup names none. NULL keeps the current default (initially the first variant attached).

overwrite

Replace the label of a (frame, member, variant) already present. FALSE (default) makes that an error.

Value

The scale with the rows added.

Details

Labels are for display. Alternative spellings to be matched belong in the alias table, see attach_aliases_scale().

See also

scale_labels(), scale_label()

Examples

s <- attach_labels_scale(
  scale_example(),
  data.frame(frame = "sector", member = c("P", "S", NA),
             label = c("Primary", "Secondary", "Sector"))
)
scale_labels(s)
#>    frame member variant     label
#> 1 sector      P   label   Primary
#> 2 sector      S   label Secondary
#> 3 sector   <NA>   label    Sector
scale_label(s, c("P", "S", "T"), frame = "sector")
#> [1] "Primary"   "Secondary" "T"
